slides.heading: Making Your Data Tell a Story
bullet_points: Python for Data Science — Tutorial 5 of 10
slides.speaker_note: Open with the central insight: your charts are evaluated before your model is — and most people find out the hard way.

slides.heading: The Problem: Default Charts Kill Good Analysis
bullet_points: Gray backgrounds, tiny fonts, cluttered axes
First impressions form before the numbers land
slides.speaker_note: Share the personal story — 0.94 R² model, default matplotlib output, feedback on the charts rather than the analysis.

slides.heading: matplotlib vs seaborn: Layers, Not Competitors
bullet_points: Seaborn is built on top of matplotlib
Seaborn for the 80%: fast, good-looking defaults
slides.speaker_note: Clarify the mental model once so people stop treating them as alternatives.

slides.heading: Setup: One Block for Every Notebook
bullet_points: Remove top + right spines — they add no information
Set figure DPI to 150 — default 72 is too low
slides.speaker_note: Walk through what each line does and show a before/after side by side.

slides.heading: The 5 Plot Types That Cover 90% of EDA
slides.speaker_note: Preview each chart type with a Titanic dataset screenshot — one image per type.

slides.heading: Combining seaborn + matplotlib: The Key Insight
bullet_points: Every seaborn call returns a matplotlib object
Use axes-level functions with explicit ax= targets
Build a full dashboard in under 25 lines
slides.speaker_note: Show the 2×2 dashboard code and resulting output side by side — this is the moment the two libraries click.

slides.heading: Three Details That Make or Break a Chart
bullet_points: Zero baseline on all bar charts — always
slides.speaker_note: Show bad vs good examples for each — these are honest mistakes almost every beginner makes.

slides.heading: Saving Publication-Quality Output
bullet_points: SVG and PDF for resolution-independent files
slides.speaker_note: Show a zoomed comparison between 72 DPI and 300 DPI on a slide — the difference is visible immediately.

slides.heading: What's Next: Statistical Testing
slides.speaker_note: Close with the series arc — they have good data and good charts; next is knowing if what they see is real.
